aspects.says: While both standards coexist, one gateway accepts either format, dispatches on which one it received and translates between them.
ISO 20022 differs from ISO-8583 above all in its data model: conceptual, logical and physical layers, where ISO-8583 describes mainly the physical message.
An ISO-8583 message can be carried as JSON or XML, as its MTI plus a map from field number to value, trading compactness for readability or schema validation.
aspects.reason: the page shows only the shape; its JSON channel needs Jackson, which a graded run does not have, and is a sketch rather than working code

aspects.says: Moving to ISO 20022 can be phased, translated, run in parallel, or done as a complete overhaul, the last being the riskiest.
aspects.reason: a list of options to weigh rather than an idea to check; the translation it relies on is part of the gateway question
